frames.narration: An order ships. The order service saves it and writes a notification request into its outbox in the same transaction, then a relay forwards the request.
The API checks the customer's preferences. They allow push, not email, and it is not quiet hours.
The user is under their daily cap, so the API fills in the template and puts one push message on the right queue. It gives the message a unique id, n-123.
A sender worker takes the message and checks the sent log. n-123 has not been sent, so it goes ahead.
The worker calls the push provider with n-123 as the idempotency key. The provider is having a bad moment and returns an error.
The worker waits a short random time (backoff with jitter) and tries again. This time the provider accepts. If it kept failing, the message would end up in the dead-letter queue.
The worker records n-123 as sent and acknowledges the message, so the queue deletes it. Had the worker crashed just before this, the redelivery would be recognised and skipped.
The provider later reports a delivery receipt, and the notification is marked delivered. The order service never waited for any of this.
